title: Tomcat cluster TLS-PSK on TLS 1.3 doesn't check the peer
why: Apache rates it Critical, but it only matters for Tomcat clusters secured with TLS 1.3 and TLS-PSK on three recent releases, and there's a simple workaround (TLS 1.2). No exploit, no reported attacks, not on CISA KEV. A page would make it look bigger than it is.
page_if: public exploit code or reported attacks, or a CISA KEV listing
a source shows the TLS-PSK cluster setup is common, or that other setups are affected
news or researcher coverage beyond aggregators and news summaries

facts.text: Apache's advisory (19 Nov 2026, Critical): a node with no credentials could join a Tomcat cluster when the cluster was secured with TLS 1.3 and TLS-PSK. Affected: 11.0.28 to 11.0.29, 10.1.62 and 9.0.124. Credited to Mike Read.
No fixed release yet: 11.0.30, 10.1.63 and 9.0.125 are listed as not yet released. Until then, Apache says to switch cluster encryption to TLS 1.2 with TLS-PSK.
Sources conflict on the 9.0 fix: the CVE record says 9.0.123, which is older than the affected 9.0.124; Apache's 9.x security page and announcement say 9.0.125.
The CVE record gives only Apache's text rating "critical", no CVSS score. No exploit code found on GitHub, and it isn't on CISA KEV (catalog of 18 Nov).

sources.title: Apache Tomcat announce list: advisory and mitigations
Apache Tomcat 10 security page: fixed in 10.1.63 (not yet released)
Apache Tomcat 9 security page: fixed in 9.0.125 (not yet released)

history.text: Covered by the [Tomcat Nov release](/tomcat-2026-11-19/) roundup, which takes in all 11 Tomcat CVEs from 19 Nov. Still no fixed release, exploit or KEV listing; CISA added a 9.8 score to the CVE record.
Evaluated: watch, no page yet. Came up in a news summary that said attackers can "join secure clusters" without the TLS 1.3 and TLS-PSK conditions.
